title: Divergence: RATIONALE cage entry misstates seccomp-BPF mechanics (claims BPF cannot read argument registers; contradicts own Direction)

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: RATIONALE 'cage' Limits: 'Classic seccomp-BPF compares seccomp_data.nr, not argument registers — so it cannot filter ioctl by its cmd... subject to TOCTOU on pointer arguments it does not inspect.' Factually wrong about the mechanism: struct seccomp_data exposes args[0..5] and classic BPF filters routinely compare argument VALUES (Chrome's sandbox filters ioctl by cmd this way). The true mechanism limit: BPF cannot DEREFERENCE pointer arguments (kernel forbids it precisely to avoid TOCTOU), so paths can't be scoped. As written it (a) attributes this filter's v0.1 implementation choice (nr-only) to seccomp-BPF itself, (b) muddles TOCTOU (BPF can't inspect pointed-to memory at all; TOCTOU is the documented reason dereference is prohibited), and (c) contradicts the entry's own Direction, which proposes 'a BPF_JEQ on the ioctl cmd register' — impossible if the mechanism 'compares only nr'. forge/src/sandbox.rs doc comment near TERM_SYSCALLS repeats the same error. An OS/systems reviewer catches this in one read.
